limits: Static metadata only; this does not prove runtime patch safety or load order behavior.
Use exact ids or signatures from code hooks before decompile or downstream notes.
topics.summary: Start from managed metadata to find likely hookable gameplay methods, then resolve one exact method signature before deeper navigation.

limits: Scene hints stay static and filesystem-oriented; live runtime trees remain under the dev surface.
Attached script ids require script metadata in the indexed assemblies.
topics.summary: Move from a scene or node into the attached managed script type, then pivot into managed hook discovery for callback methods.

limits: Assets extract artifacts; scene/resource inspection keeps structured metadata. Treat them as separate surfaces.
Not every asset resolves to one owning script; confirm broader references before patching.
topics.summary: Use asset extraction and static scene/resource inspection together to trace a visual asset back to the script or scene that likely controls it.

limits: M32 does not add live hook probing or runtime patch verification.
Use runtime/dev commands as confirmatory evidence, not as a replacement for static signature resolution.
topics.summary: Confirm static hook research with existing live diagnostics, runtime scene inspection, screenshots, or extracted artifacts without adding a new hook-probing surface.

limits: This is authoring guidance over the installed game API; exact type and method names must be confirmed with code locate, refs, describe, or decompile.
Runtime validation should use fixtures, state, diagnostics, logs, screenshots, or test scenarios rather than hidden combat-state mutation.
topics.summary: Research combat intents, command APIs, combat state, card piles, and the action queue before writing combat-affecting mod logic.

limits: This topic does not generate source files or prescribe one project layout.
Community libraries may change registration details; inspect the target mod dependencies before assuming BaseLib or raw-game patterns.
topics.summary: Understand STS2 entity models, stable IDs, pools, localization, and examples before adding cards, relics, powers, potions, monsters, encounters, events, or modifiers.

limits: spirectl does not depend on BaseLib and does not guarantee BaseLib availability in a target mod.
Confirm package versions, namespaces, attributes, and pool registration in the target project or installed mod assemblies before editing code.
topics.summary: Use BaseLib references as optional community-library guidance for custom models, pools, dynamic variables, config, custom enums, and common namespace pitfalls.

limits: Hook and patch suitability is advisory until exact signatures and call sites are resolved against the installed game assemblies.
Transpilers and private reflection are brittle and should be last-resort choices with explicit validation.
topics.summary: Choose between native hooks, BaseLib hooks, Harmony prefix/postfix patches, transpilers, reflection, or no patch before changing game behavior.

limits: This is reference-only; spirectl does not add PCK packaging or source-writing helpers in this topic.
dotnet build only builds a PCK when the mod project has explicit MSBuild targets or scripts for that behavior.
topics.summary: Research res:// assets, embedded resources, localization files, optional PCK wiring, Godot scene script registration, and programmatic UI before adding visual or UI mod code.

limits: Single-player behavior is not enough proof for multiplayer-safe mod logic.
A local bridge perspective can validate observable state and ownership metadata, but it does not create independent remote clients.
topics.summary: Keep mod behavior deterministic and multiplayer-aware by researching game RNG streams, save/load effects, authority, message shapes, and ownership boundaries.

limits: Troubleshooting entries are starting points; always inspect the first real compiler error, game log exception, or bridge diagnostic notice before editing.
This topic does not add automatic repair or source mutation helpers.
topics.summary: Map common mod build, load, registration, localization, asset, hook, and runtime failures to likely causes and the next spirectl inspection command.

limits: Fixtures are recipe-backed setup, not hidden runtime restore; they do not patch combat queues, RNG continuation, animation state, enemy AI history, or transient UI internals.
Shareable dev.load-scenario sparse artifacts and exact native sidecars are separate restore surfaces.
Local-only degraded multiplayer fixtures model the local bridge perspective and omitted remote clients; they do not create fake remote clients.
topics.summary: Use authored .sts2.fixture.yaml recipes for deterministic screen-entry setup and read recipeReport diagnostics for applied, inferred, omitted, unsupported, degraded multiplayer, and bridge-validation fields.

limits: Native STS2 mod loading remains startup-bound; shell or patch signature changes still require restart.
M57 exposes the template and reference workflow only; CLI reload automation is deferred to M61.
topics.summary: Build a stable Harmony shell that owns patch methods and reloads developer-owned logic through a collectible contract-bound assembly.
